store.0: MD of Legend Investments. Focus: AI-driven trading & ESG investing. Principles: foresight, precision, adaptability. Responsibilities: strategy, risk management, institutional clients. Reputation: analytical rigor, spotting opportunities where others see obstacles.
store.1: Active deals: $8.5B QuantumChip-Silicon Core(U.S.-China regs). $3.2B VertexSoft LBO(debt structuring). $5B+ Solaris-Nordic Renewables(incentive alignment). Weekly 7 AM Monday call(Asian markets). Potential $20B Omnix AI take-private(game-changer).
store.2: Education: B.S. Economics(Penn); MBA(Harvard, Baker Scholar). Active in academia: guest lecturing, mentoring, recruiting. Endowed Penn scholarship for first-gen finance students. Belief: talent is greatest investment; finance should be accessible to all through hunger and discipline.

store.0: Key landmark deals: 2019 Poison Pill defense of Surreal Incorporated(mid-cap tech) - became Harvard Business School case study. $8.6B cross-border semiconductor merger between Nexa Semiconductors and Taihua Microelectronics - taught that global finance requires diplomacy as much as numbers. $14.2B healthcare merger between BioCrest Labs and OncoPharm Therapeutics - nearly collapsed twice on IP valuation and regulatory approval; resolved after 3 sleepless days; WSJ called it 'the deal that reshaped modern cancer treatment.' Personal memento: lucite from first $500M transaction(funded Stratos Aerospace expansion) remains on desk as a daily reminder to apply the same energy and determination to every deal, regardless of size.
store.1: Career journey: Began as analyst at Goldman Sachs(2001) - gained experience in M&A modeling and survived the dot-com crash. Moved to Morgan Stanley(2004) - worked on early social media tech deals as associate. Promoted to Vice President at 31 - led defining transactions of that era. Joined Legend Investments in 2015 as Managing Director - first major transaction: NeuralNet Systems IPO(largest tech IPO to date). Built a reputation for handling complex, cross-border deals. Core principle: trust is earned through track record and network, not promises.
